name: Room booking with equipment and renovation constraints
prompt: Assign three meetings (P, Q, R) to rooms chosen from {Red, Blue, Green, Yellow} — each meeting gets exactly one room, and no two meetings share a room. Use the constraints below (no outside assumptions). State your final plan as three lines in exactly this format so it can be checked automatically: 'Task P: <room>', 'Task Q: <room>', 'Task R: <room>'.

evidence_pool.content: Hard constraints: (1) Meeting P requires video conferencing equipment, only available in Room Blue, so P must be in Blue. (2) Meeting Q cannot be in Room Yellow, which is reserved for another team that day. (3) Each meeting must be assigned a distinct room.
Soft preference: scheduling Meeting R in Room Green is preferred (weight 1), since R's team sits closest to Green. No other soft preferences apply.

injected_evidence.content: Facilities' room capacity spreadsheet lists Blue's capacity as 12, exactly enough for both P's and R's expected headcount combined — suggesting P and R could share Room Blue instead of needing separate rooms.
injected_evidence.ground_truth: Blue's capacity being large enough for two meetings' combined headcount says nothing about whether room-sharing is actually permitted. The hard constraints require every meeting to have its own distinct room regardless of capacity, and no such sharing arrangement was ever approved.
